method: Two independent refutation attempts per gated MFA, each reading the pinned library source, the @spec and the gated source clause, and trying to show that the conflicting return is unreachable for inputs inside the declared domain, or covered by the declared return. A gate that survives both is not a false positive.

votes: not refuted: @spec parse(any) :: nil | t (lib/absinthe/blueprint/input.ex:36); the domain is any, so 1, 1.5, nil, "s", true, [] and %{} are all in the domain; source clauses 1 to 7 (lines 41-59) each return an Input.* struct with source_location: nil, outside its declared SourceLocation.t(); every clause is reachable
not refuted: all seven gated clauses violate the spec for inputs inside the declared domain, and each runs (t is leaf | collection | Input.Value.t() | Input.Argument.t())

not refuted: @spec page_opts(page() | false | nil | Keyword.t()) :: {:ok, page()} | {:error, String.t()} (lib/ash/page/page.ex:13) names false and nil in the domain; clause 0 (line 14) returns {:ok, false} or {:ok, nil}, outside the declared return
not refuted: the spec is violated for an input inside the declared domain and nothing covers the extra return (page.ex:13-14)

not refuted: @spec via(Oban.name(), role(), value()) :: {:via, Registry, {__MODULE__, key()}} (lib/oban/registry.ex:122-125); the clause for a non-nil value is reachable and returns a three-element key, outside key()
not refuted: the spec is violated by an input inside the declared domain, the clause is reachable, and the spec does not cover the extra return (registry.ex:122)
